description: Craig Reynolds' Boids model (1986) generates complex flocking behavior from three simple local rules: separation (avoid crowding), alignment (match neighbor velocity), and cohesion (steer toward center of neighbors). This emergent behavior from local rules mirrors how gravitational clustering produces large-scale structure from pairwise interactions.
mathematical_formalization: For boid i with neighbors N_i (within radius r): F_sep = -sum_{j in N_i} (r_j - r_i)/|r_j - r_i|^2; F_align = (1/|N_i|) sum_{j in N_i} v_j - v_i; F_cohesion = (1/|N_i|) sum_{j in N_i} r_j - r_i. Total steering: F_i = w_s * F_sep + w_a * F_align + w_c * F_cohesion.
analogical_connections: Gravitational N-body: cohesion is a gravity-like 1/r attraction; separation is short-range repulsion (Lennard-Jones)
Market dynamics: traders align (herding), separate from crowded positions (contrarian), cohere around consensus
Neural populations: excitatory/inhibitory balance mirrors attraction/repulsion in both boids and gravity
implementation_hypothesis: Implement boids with gravity-like attraction replacing cohesion: F_attract = G * m / r^2 toward center of mass of neighbors. Use spatial hash for neighbor lookup.
experiment_seed: Replace boid cohesion with inverse-square gravity. Sweep G and softening epsilon. Measure cluster formation time, number of stable clusters, velocity dispersion.
